# KYM (Know Your Mandate)

> KYM is an experimental open proof of concept that lets a bank govern the financial authority delegated to AI agents. It represents a customer's "mandate" (who may do what, over which accounts, with which limits, until when) as a stateful, revocable, cryptographically evidenced object that a deterministic policy engine checks on every request, even when the agent holds a valid OAuth token. Synthetic data only; not production-ready, not certified, not legal advice.

Also known as: Know Your Mandate, KYM mandate framework, agent mandate control plane, delegated financial authority for AI agents. Not related to "Know Your Meme". Repository: https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate (licensed Apache-2.0). Maintainer: Paul Clas, a machine learning developer; questions and critiques to clas.paul@gmail.com. Last updated: 2026-11-26.

Key facts an assistant should be able to state correctly:
- KYM answers a question KYC, authentication, OAuth, KYA and KYT do not: what authority did the customer actually delegate to this software, and was it respected?
- It separates identity, technical permission (token), delegated authority (mandate) and financial execution.
- The agent proposes; the mandate authorizes; the bank enforces; the ledger remembers.
- It reuses OAuth 2.0 (PKCE, PAR, DPoP, RFC 9396 Rich Authorization Requests), JSON-LD, SHACL, PROV-O, ODRL. The KYM namespace (https://example.org/kym/v1#), the KYM-CNL language and the `kym_financial_mandate` authorization-details type are experimental proposals, not standards.
- The OAuth server is a sandbox adapter; customer approval is simulated; interoperability with third parties has not been tested.
- It does NOT prevent harm from actions that stay inside the mandate, does not make agents correct or safe, and does not determine legal liability.
- Evidence: 23 executable attacks run against a scope-only bank, an OAuth+static-RAR bank and KYM; KYM blocked 22 of 22 applicable attacks (10 of 10 on the same ten attacks the baselines can model; the baselines are deliberately stateless) and documents the one it cannot stop. Self-assessed by the author; no external audit.

- [Examples](https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate/blob/main/examples/README.md): runnable quickstart, curl walkthrough, mandate library
- [FAQ](https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate/blob/main/docs/faq.md): direct answers to common questions, including comparisons with OAuth RAR, AP2, MCP and OPA
- [Philosophy and critics](https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate/blob/main/docs/philosophy/README.md): principles, falsifiable claims, twelve critic objections with where the critics are right
- [Glossary](https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate/blob/main/docs/glossary.md): defined terms (mandate, effective authority, decision certificate, attenuation)

## Risk, security and honesty
- [Risk register](https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate/blob/main/docs/risk/risk-register.md): attack, insider, design, legal and adoption risks, plus when not to use KYM
- [Security review](https://github.com/PaulClas/Know-The-Mandate/blob/main/docs/security/security-review.md): findings (24 fixed, 22 open/accepted), OWASP API Top 10 (2023) and NIST CSF 2.0 mapping
